title_prefix: ms-produce-input has no multi_a case, so
mechanism: The ECASE in MS-PRODUCE-INPUT (src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1500, inside the defun at :1491) enumerates 26 fragments and omits :MULTI-A, while every other half of the implementation handles it: the fragment list (miniscript.lisp:75), the type calculus (:386), script generation (:547-555), CalcOps (:761), CalcStackSize (:826), CalcWitnessSize (:918), the string parser (:1214-1222) and the printer (:1305). So a multi_a node parses, types, compiles and sizes, and fails only when something asks it for a witness -- and it fails as SB-KERNEL:CASE-FAILURE, a hard error, not as a graceful 'no satisfaction' NIL. Core's ProduceInput has a MULTI_A arm (refs/bitcoin/src/script/miniscript.h:1259-1284) with its own dynamic program that differs from MULTI in three ways: it signs keys in REVERSE order (node.keys[n-1-i], because CHECKSIGADD reads the first key's signature from the top of the stack), it starts sats[0] at EMPTY rather than at ZERO (there is no CHECKMULTISIG off-by-one element to absorb), and its dissatisfaction is as many empty vectors as there are keys.
consequence: Latent today for the same reason as 8c3b8174, and confirmed latent by grep: MS-SATISFY has one caller in src/, src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:472, and it is only reached with a node that MS-FROM-SCRIPT produced from a P2WSH witnessScript -- a context in which multi_a cannot occur, and which the decoder could not produce anyway since it has no MULTI_A arm. No wrong satisfaction reaches the wallet's own flow today, so S3 stands. The consequence is entirely about ordering and about the FAILURE MODE: the moment ms-satisfy is wired to tr() leaves (the 1141db2b fix), a multi_a leaf answers with an unhandled CASE-FAILURE rather than an unsigned input, which surfaces to the operator as RPC -32603 'internal error' instead of 'complete: false'. Note the ordering is strict: fixing 8c3b8174 alone MAKES this reachable, because a decoded MULTI_A node would then be handed straight to ms-satisfy.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-miniscript-s3, warm image, probe build/ga11probe/p2.lisp (git-ignored) run twice with identical results. One ms-satisfier with a constant 64-byte sign-fn drives all five cases, so a failure cannot be a fixture artifact. Well-formed controls in the SAME context through the SAME fixture: pk(K1) :TAPSCRIPT -> (:OK (64)); and_v(v:pk(K1),pk(K2)) :TAPSCRIPT -> (:OK (64 64)); multi(1,K1,K2) :P2WSH -> (:OK (0 64)), the leading 0 being the CHECKMULTISIG dummy. Cases under test: multi_a(1,K1,K2) :TAPSCRIPT and multi_a(2,K1,K2) :TAPSCRIPT both -> (:ERROR SB-KERNEL:CASE-FAILURE ":MULTI-A fell through ECASE expression. Wanted one of (:JUST-0 :JUST-1 :PK-K :PK-H :OLDER :AFTER :SHA256 :RIPEMD160 :HASH256 :HASH160 :WRAP-A :WRAP-S :WRAP-C :WRAP-N :WRAP-D :WRAP-V :WRAP-J :AND-V :AND-B :OR-B :OR-C :OR-D :OR-I :ANDOR :MULTI :THRESH)."). Reachability grep: 'ms-satisfy' appears in src/ only at src/rpc/rawtransaction.lisp:472 and in src/validation/package.lisp:202. Core side read at d3056bc: refs/bitcoin/src/script/miniscript.h:1259-1284 (MULTI_A) against :1285-1310 (MULTI), which is where the reversed key order and the EMPTY-vs-ZERO seed are visible side by side. Ours: src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1491 (defun), :1500 (the ECASE).
fix_shape: Add a :MULTI-A clause to the ECASE at src/validation/miniscript.lisp:1500, next to the existing :MULTI clause, transcribing miniscript.h:1259-1284 rather than editing a copy of :MULTI -- the three differences are exactly the parts a copy gets wrong. Seed sats with a single (ms-stack-empty), not (ms-stack-zero). Iterate i over the keys and sign (nth (- nkeys 1 i) keys), not (nth i keys). Build next-sats as: element 0 is (ms-stack+ sats[0] (ms-stack-zero)); for j from 1 below (length sats), (ms-stack-or (ms-stack+ sats[j] (ms-stack-zero)) (ms-stack+ sats[j-1] sat)); then push (ms-stack+ sats[last] sat). Return (values sats[k] sats[0]). Assert k /= 0 the way Core's CHECK_NONFATAL does. The regression oracle already exists and must be used, because it pins the element order this clause has to reproduce: the tapscript multi_a arm of tr-leaf-satisfaction (src/rpc/descriptors.lisp:1369-1425) and its test tests/wallet/descriptor-tests.lisp tr-script-path-spends-verify produce a working multi_a witness today, so the ported clause must yield the same stack for the same keys before 1141db2b deletes that hand-rolled arm.
